title: EBT fraud scheme stole more than $7 million in SNAP benefits in New York - ABC7 New York
text:
EBT fraud scheme stole more than $7 million in SNAP benefits in New York - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut EBT 'fraud factory' scheme stole more than $7 million in SNAP benefits 
 Anthony Carlo has more on the alleged scheme. AP Photo/Damian Dovarganes By Anthony Carlo Friday, October 30, 2026 3:39AM Share Follow abc7NY on Google NEW YORK (WABC) -- A group of defendants accused of operating what prosecutors described as a "fraud factory" stole more than $7 million in SNAP benefits by repeatedly using stolen EBT card information, according to the Manhattan District Attorney's Office.
 Prosecutors allege the scheme targeted low-income New Yorkers who rely on food assistance benefits, draining funds intended to help them buy food. Authorities say the stolen benefits were converted into cash and used to purchase luxury vehicles.
 "They were people who were going to withdraw funds using an EBT card and the money was gone," a law enforcement official said.
 According to court documents, the defendants are accused of conspiring to "steal more than $7 million" by "using the names of existing or fictitious delis to obtain credit card and EBT processing accounts."
 Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said investigators allege the defendants obtained EBT card information and waited for benefits to be deposited before transferring the funds.
 "And then they were, we allege, skimming or otherwise stealing the card information and then just waiting to the day when the cards got loaded with new funds and then just swiping the cards right into their own accounts," Bragg said.
 Prosecutors allege the defendants targeted thousands of victims over a two-year period, stealing SNAP benefits and sending some of the proceeds to Yemen.
 Three of the eight defendants were arraigned Thursday on grand larceny and other charges, including the alleged leader of the operation. The defendants pleaded not guilty.
 "According to the district attorney he is the leader of this alleged conspiracy. That remains to be seen," defense attorney Michael Farkas said.
 The case comes months after the U.S. Secret Service demonstrated how criminals can install skimming devices at bodegas and other stores during a June crackdown on EBT-related fraud in New York City.
 Experts advise EBT cardholders to check whether card readers appear loose or tampered with, change their EBT PINs monthly and remember that state agencies will never call or text requesting a PIN.
 The investigation and prosecution remain ongoing.
